clinician.trajectory_summary: An 80-year-old man presented with frontal headaches and bilateral jaw pain with claudication. Initial CT head was unremarkable. Physical examination revealed bilateral tender, nodular, and weakly pulsatile temporal arteries. Inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR) were not significantly raised. A temporal and axillary artery ultrasound showed a characteristic positive halo sign in the right temporal artery. A subsequent right temporal artery biopsy revealed a muscular artery with focal adventitial chronic inflammation and intimal hyperplasia with mild inflammation, which was consistent with Giant Cell Arteritis (GCA).

A right temporal artery biopsy (TAB) revealed a muscular artery with focal adventitial chronic inflammation and intimal hyperplasia with mild inflammation.
The biopsy findings were consistent with GCA.
